children: Poland’s leading medical diagnostic and laboratory company Diagnostyka
reported on Thursday a 10% fall in second-quarter net profit as surging costs outpaced rising revenue driven by higher volumes and prices of diagnostic tests and services.
The company continued its expansion strategy, with its laboratory network increasing to 157 nationwide, complemented by its about 1,300 collection points.
The company's net profit attributable to shareholders fell to 57.4 million zlotys  ($15.4 million) in the second quarter, while revenue grew 15.6% to 686.2 million zlotys, it said.
"Thanks to dynamic organic growth and selective acquisitions, the Diagnostyka Group has strengthened its market position," deputy CFO Bartosz Cieslicki said.
The company said higher sales were driven by an increase in both the volume and prices of its tests.
The average price of diagnostic services rose 11.9% year-on-year in the first half of the year.
The company's total volume of tests performed increased 2.6% year-on-year in the first half, reaching 91.3 million.
